heroHeadline: Battle of Bhamo: KIA Coalition Presses Siege as SAC Conducts 50 Airstrikes/Day — Min Aung Hlaing in Mumbai; TNLA Namhkam Explosion Kills 43–55 — Day 1,947
heroSubtitle: On Day 1,947 (June 2, 2026), the Battle of Bhamo has intensified into Myanmar's most decisive ongoing conventional engagement: the KIA-led coalition maintains its siege of the SAC-held Kachin State city while the junta conducts up to 50 airstrikes per day — the highest concentration of SAC air power observed in Kachin State since the coup — in a desperate bid to hold the city against encirclement. If Bhamo falls, the KIA would control all of eastern Kachin State. Simultaneously, Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing is in Mumbai for a business and industry forum on Day 4 of his five-day India state visit (May 30–June 3) — the diplomatic centerpiece of the week following his June 1 bilateral summit with PM Modi. The week's deadliest discrete incident was not a junta airstrike but an accidental explosion of TNLA-stored mining explosives at Kaung Tat village, Namhkam Township, Shan State on June 1, killing between 43 and 55 people including at least 6 children. In Rakhine, the Arakan Army has advanced to within 5km of Kyaukphyu's Chinese-backed CMEC port, the AA has killed 40+ junta soldiers in fighting near Sittwe's naval bases (May 29–June 1), and junta warships from Danyawaddy naval base continue shelling the area. IDP figures have accelerated to approximately 5.2 million — the highest since the 2021 coup — with 16.2 million requiring humanitarian assistance. The five-front war (Rakhine, Kachin, Sagaing, Chin, Karen/Tanintharyi) continues unabated.
